_strings.@@2982a8bca499: Treaty conformity — OR conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from OR income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the OR return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Oregon's resident return (Form OR-40) starts from federal adjusted gross income: 2024 Form OR-40 line 7 is "Federal adjusted gross income (AGI). Enter your federal AGI from Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 11; or Form 1040-X, line 1C." Oregon taxable income is then built by applying additions (Schedule OR-ASC) and subtractions to that federal AGI. The 2024 OR-40 instruction booklet contains no general addition/add-back of federally treaty-exempt income (unlike California's Schedule CA, or CT/MD/MS). Because federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI on the 1040 and there is no Oregon add-back code restoring it, the treaty exclusion flows through and is NOT re-taxed by Oregon -> conforms. Caveat: confirm against the full Schedule OR-ASC / OR-ASC-NP addition code list and Publication OR-17 for any niche addition that could touch a specific treaty article.

_strings.@@ebef57d8f72a: Oregon Earned Income Credit (EIC) — You must qualify for the federal Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC). Low- to moderate-income working individuals and families. state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form OR-40, line 20 "Tax (see instructions)". Instructions p.16: "Tax tables. Use the tax tables to find your tax if your taxable income on line 19 is less than $50,000." and "Tax rate charts. If your taxable income on line 19 is $50,000 or more, calculate your tax using the formula in the tax rate chart for your filing status. Use Chart S if your filing status is single or married filing separately. Use Chart J if your filing status is married filing jointly, head of household, or qualifying surviving spouse." This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply 2024 Form OR-40, line 15 "Income after subtractions" (line 9 income after additions minus line 14 total subtractions). Line 15 already reflects Oregon additions (Schedule OR-ASC) and all subtractions, including the line 10 federal tax liability subtraction (2024 limit $8,250; $4,125 married filing separately; phased down by federal AGI per Table 4 — $0 at AGI of $145,000+ single/MFS or $290,000+ MFJ/HoH/QSS). The op subtracts only the Table 5 standard deduction to reach line 19 (Oregon taxable income) and applies the rate schedule. Filers who itemize for Oregon (line 16 Schedule OR-A amount larger than the standard deduction) or who claim the age-65+/blind additional standard deduction must compute lines 17-19 on the form instead — the op models only the basic per-status standard deduction. Adjudication note (two-pass): base is federal_agi — Form OR-40 line 7 is federal adjusted gross income; supply the pre-deduction Oregon income figure (line 19 taxable income = line 15 minus the line 16/17 deduction is what the op reproduces by subtracting the standard deduction). Vector counts are zero by design: Oregon personal/dependent exemptions are the $249-per-exemption CREDIT on line 25 (2024, up from $236 in 2023), income-limited, never a base reduction. 2024 indexing verified across three documents: OR-40 booklet charts ($50,000+ segments), OR-40-N/P instructions (full four-bracket charts), and Publication OR-ESTIMATE (full charts) — all agree on $4,300/$10,750/$125,000 (S) and $8,600/$21,500/$250,000 (J). Tax-table mandate below $50,000: the 2024 OR-40 instructions (line 20, p.16) REQUIRE the tax tables when Oregon taxable income (line 19) is less than $50,000 — the table is built from the rounded chart constants at $100-band midpoints, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within a band (booklet Example 1: single, taxable income $19,525 — table tax $1,409 vs. pure bracket math $1,409.63 -> $1,410); the filed form must use the table. The rate-chart formula applies only at $50,000 or more. Rounded printed constants: Chart S's published '$X plus Y% of excess' constants are the exact cumulative bracket sums rounded DOWN ($204 vs $204.25; $639 vs $639.625; $10,636 vs $10,636.50; the $50,000+ segment prints $4,073 vs $4,074.00 exact), so pure marginal bracket math (what this op computes) can be up to $1 HIGHER than the printed chart formula. Chart J's constants are rounded UP ($409 vs $408.50; $1,280 vs $1,279.25; $21,274 vs $21,273.00; the $50,000+ segment prints $3,774 vs $3,773.00 exact), so chart-formula results can be up to $1 higher than marginal math (booklet Example 2: MFJ $75,500 — chart $6,005 vs marginal math $6,004.25 -> $6,004). One schedule covers married filing jointly, head of household, AND qualifying surviving spouse (Chart J / tax-table Column J) — head of household brackets are identical to MFJ, and qualifying surviving spouse maps to married_filing_jointly with no divergence. Single and married filing separately share Chart S / Column S. Oregon registered domestic partners (RDPs) use the married statuses. Oregon's personal/dependent exemption is a tax CREDIT, not a base reduction, and is NOT shipped as an exemption: Form OR-40 line 25 'Exemption credit' = $249 per exemption for 2024 (taxpayer, spouse, dependents, plus severely-disabled and disabled-child exemptions), subtracted from tax after the rate applies; it is $0 when federal AGI exceeds $200,000 ($100,000 if single or married filing separately). The calc op does not model this credit. Standard-deduction gates NOT modeled: married filing separately gets $0 if the other spouse claims itemized deductions; a non-U.S. citizen without permanent resident status gets $0 (but may itemize); a person claimable as a dependent on another return is limited to the larger of earned income + $450 or $1,300, capped at the basic amount for their status. Compute those cases on the form. Age 65+/blind additional standard deduction NOT modeled: each applicable checkbox below line 17 adds $1,200 (single or head of household) or $1,000 (all other filers) to the Table 5 standard deduction (booklet example: MFJ couple with one spouse 65+ enters $6,495 = $5,495 + $1,000) — enter it on the form; this op applies only the basic per-status amount. Federal tax liability subtraction is already inside the caller-supplied base (OR-40 line 10 flows into line 15): 2024 limit $8,250 ($4,125 married filing separately), phased down by federal AGI per Table 4 (single: $8,250 under $125,000 stepping to $0 at $145,000+; MFS: $4,125 stepping to $0 at $145,000+; MFJ/HoH/QSS: $8,250 under $250,000 stepping to $0 at $290,000+). NO kicker on the 2024 return: Oregon's surplus (kicker) credit is claimed on odd-year returns (44.28% on 2023 returns; the next on 2025 returns) — the 2024 booklet has no kicker line and the word does not appear. Alternative tax computations on line 20 NOT modeled: Schedule OR-FIA-40 (farm income averaging, box 20a), Worksheet FCG in Publication OR-FCG (farm asset capital gain rate, box 20b), and Schedule OR-PTE-FY (qualified business income reduced tax rate, box 20c — irrevocable election) replace the table/chart math when elected. Bracket source: the OR-40 booklet (p.28) prints Chart S/Chart J only for taxable income of $50,000 or more (the tables govern below); the full four-bracket 2024 Chart S/Chart J including the $4,300/$10,750 and $8,600/$21,500 breakpoints is printed in the 2024 Form OR-40-N/OR-40-P instructions (150-101-048-1, Rev. 10-16-24) and in 2024 Publication OR-ESTIMATE (150-101-026), p.3: https://www.oregon.gov/dor/forms/FormsPubs/publication-or-estimate_101-026_2024.pdf — spot-checks of the booklet's tax tables (e.g., Column S at $19,500-$19,600 = $1,409; Column S at $49,900-$50,000 = $4,069; Column J at $9,700-$9,800 = $487) match this schedule chained from the printed constants.
